questions: What is the matched launch and grid-wave envelope?
What is the marginal service time of a necessary block barrier?
What contiguous cache-resident global-load issue service is achieved?
What contiguous global-store issue service is achieved?

modes.launch: One live sink store per thread with configurable launch geometry and dynamic shared allocation.
modes.barrier: Each repeat writes a unique shared page, synchronizes, then reads a peer value; one required barrier per repeat.
modes.load: Each repeat reads an independent contiguous uint4 bank and consumes every value in a per-thread checksum.
modes.store: Each repeat writes an independent contiguous uint4 bank.

measurement_semantics.timing_scope: GPU-active native CUDA graph replay measured by CUDA events and divided by the number of identical kernel nodes.
measurement_semantics.cache_state: Warm by default; working-set size is explicit and a cache-level claim requires separate cache-control evidence.
measurement_semantics.repetitions: A configurable repeat count creates a service curve; zero-repeat controls are retained.
measurement_semantics.launch_geometry: Grid, block and dynamic shared-memory allocation are explicit inputs.

correctness_controls: copy the live sink or destination to the host after timing and checksum it
require monotonic work and expected output changes across repeat counts
dce_guard: Live global sink or destination is copied back after timing and checksummed.

constraints: CUDA runtime and a compatible CUDA compiler

known_pollution: graph replay overhead divided by node count
barrier includes one shared store and one peer shared load per repeat
warm repetitions are normally cache resident unless the working set exceeds cache
claims_allowed: service curves for the recorded geometry, source and environment
relative local slopes when monotonicity and correctness pass
claims_forbidden: absolute DRAM bandwidth without cache-control evidence
production operator lower bound without matched production geometry and layout
